title: Stock Rally As Powell Sparks A Buying Frenzy
summary:
By Lance Roberts
The latest FOMC meeting caused a stock rally as Jerome Powell turned more “dovish” than expected. While Powell did note that progress on inflation has been lackluster, the announcement of the reversal of “Quantitative Tightening” (QT) excited the bulls.
Beginning in June, the Committee will slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $60 billion to $25 billion. The Committee will maintain the monthly redemption cap on agency debt and agency mortgage‑backed securities at $35 billion and will reinvest any principal payments in excess of this cap into Treasury securities”

Of course, the reversal of QT means a buyer of Treasury bonds is returning to the market, increasing overall market liquidity. It also means the Treasury will issue $105 billion less in gross in Q3. The bond market also got the memo, as the Fed’s return to the bond market suggests lower yields in the months ahead, easing financing pressure in the economy.
We have previously discussed the following chart of “liquidity,” which subtracts the Treasury General Account and Reverse Repo from the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet. The recent market decline coincided with a sharp drop in liquidity as the TGA account surged to almost $1 trillion from April tax receipts. Over the next few months, that liquidity in the TGA will get released into the economy. At the same time, the Federal Reserve will reduce its balance sheet runoff, which will further add to overall liquidity.

Notably, the market has weathered the reduction in liquidity to date. While higher rates and the reversal of “Quantitative Easing” led to a 20% market decline in 2022, investors began to “front run” the Fed in anticipation of rate cuts and a return to balance sheet expansion.

Given that “QE” programs increase bank reserves by crediting their reserve accounts for bonds bought, the introduction of the tapering of “QT” is the first step in increasing system liquidity.

The dual-class share structure would allow Musk to control board elections and removals if he maintains significant Class B shareholdings, effectively making him irremovable without his consent. This structure limits investor influence over corporate matters.

title: Google 'Proudly' Defends Pentagon AI Ties Amid Internal Backlash: Report
summary: Google's leadership defended the company's partnership with the Pentagon to develop AI for military use, despite over 600 employees urging CEO Sundar Pichai to halt the collaboration. Alphabet president Kent Walker stated Google supports defense agencies 'proudly' and responsibly, citing past involvement in classified government work. However, employees and DeepMind researchers have raised concerns that reduced oversight of advanced AI could enable dangerous uses including domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons.

title: Meet the Company That's Quintupled Its Share of AI Chip Shipments in 2 Years
summary: Amazon has dramatically increased its share of AI chip shipments from 1.4% in Q1 2024 to 7.5% in Q4 2025, with its custom chip business reaching a $20 billion annual run rate and growing at triple-digit rates. The company's Trainium and Inferentia chips are positioned to significantly reduce capital expenditures and improve margins as adoption scales, while Nvidia remains the market leader but faces growing competition from hyperscaler custom accelerators.

title: Clink Launches the World's First Fiat Agentic Payment Skill, Letting Any Merchant Get Paid by AI Agents
summary: Clink, an AI-native payments infrastructure company, launched the world's first fiat agentic payment skill enabling autonomous AI agents to make real-currency payments on users' credit cards within pre-defined limits. Early merchant partners ModelMax and PollyReach are now live, with public access open to merchants and AI builders worldwide.

title: S&P 500 Resilience Persists Even as Underlying Momentum Fades
summary: The S&P 500 is consolidating after recent tech earnings, showing resilience despite headwinds including rising oil prices, higher bond yields, and a hawkish Fed stance that has eliminated rate cut expectations. While the index is holding support levels, momentum has stalled and the rally appears increasingly dependent on AI-driven institutional flows into mega-cap tech stocks. Technical consolidation between 7000-7043 suggests a pause rather than a reversal.

title: Microsoft Doubles Down On Agentic AI, Custom Chips And Data Center Surge As Q3 Results Shine
summary: Microsoft reported strong Q3 results with AI business surpassing $37 billion in annual recurring revenue. CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's strategy centered on 'agentic computing' and announced plans to double data center footprint within two years. Microsoft is investing in custom silicon (Maia 200 and Cobalt) while integrating hardware from partners, achieving 40% improvement in AI inference throughput. The company is scaling AI platforms like Foundry and Fabric with strong enterprise adoption.

title: Stock Market Today: Dow Jones, S&P 500 Futures Gain As Trump Weighs 'Short And Powerful' Iran Strikes— Alphabet, Meta, Amazon In Focus (UPDATED)
summary: U.S. stock futures showed mixed performance on Thursday as the Fed maintained interest rates at 3.50%-3.75%. Tech stocks led gains with Amazon, Alphabet, and Apple posting strong earnings results, while Microsoft and Meta raised capital expenditure guidance despite stock declines. Geopolitical tensions over potential Iran strikes and persistent inflation concerns tempered broader market sentiment.

title: The 'Prove It' Quarter: How Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, And Alphabet Backed AI Capex With Real Run Rates
summary: Major tech hyperscalers Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet demonstrated in their latest earnings that massive AI capital expenditures are generating substantial real revenue, not speculation. The companies reported combined AI revenue run rates exceeding $100 billion annually, backed by signed customer commitments totaling hundreds of billions. The next phase will focus on autonomous 'agentic' AI systems that execute complex tasks.

title: Which iShares Tech ETF Is Better to Invest in Artificial Intelligence (AI), SOXX or IYW?
summary: The article compares two iShares tech ETFs for AI investment: SOXX (Semiconductor ETF) offers concentrated exposure to chipmakers with higher volatility and stronger 1-year returns (148%), while IYW (U.S. Technology ETF) provides broader tech sector diversification with lower risk. SOXX has a lower expense ratio (0.34% vs 0.38%) and higher dividend yield (0.5% vs 0.1%), but IYW offers reduced volatility and exposure to non-semiconductor AI players like Alphabet.

title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg Just Delivered Great News for Nvidia and Micron Investors
summary: Meta raised its capital expenditure forecast to $125-145 billion (from $115-135 billion), citing higher component costs, particularly memory pricing. This signals continued strong AI spending across hyperscalers, with Google Cloud growing 63%, Azure up 39%, and AWS at 28%. Nvidia and Micron are positioned to benefit from increased capex and higher chip prices, which improve margins. The commentary suggests the AI investment boom is still in early stages with several more years of growth expected.

title: Alphabet's 'Phenomenal' Quarter Powers Biggest Stock Breakout Since 2004
summary: Alphabet reported strong Q1 results with $109.9B revenue (up 22% YoY), 19% Search growth, and 63% Google Cloud growth to $20B. The company's Cloud backlog nearly doubled to $460B, demonstrating successful AI monetization. The stock surged 7.8% and is on track for its best month since October 2004. Multiple Wall Street analysts raised price targets, with most maintaining bullish ratings as AI investments show concrete returns.

title: Meta Posted Its Best Sales Growth Since 2021—So Why Did Shares Fall?
summary: Meta reported strong Q1 2026 earnings with 33% revenue growth to $56.31B and 62% EPS growth, beating analyst expectations. However, shares fell ~7-8% after-hours due to raised CapEx guidance of $125-145B (up from $115-135B), driven by higher component pricing and data center costs. While the company's advertising business remains strong and new AI model Muse Spark was released, investors remain concerned about AI investment returns and unclear monetization of AI products.

title: Stock Market Today: Dow Jones Roars As Industrials Rescue Wall Street From Meta-Led Tech Slide
summary: The Dow Jones surged 1.5% driven by industrial and healthcare stocks, while mega-cap tech faced pressure from concerns over AI capital spending. Meta and Microsoft declined on capex worries, but Alphabet gained on enterprise AI wins. Industrials like Caterpillar, Quanta Services, and Carrier rallied on data-center infrastructure demand. The S&P 500 gained 0.5% while the Nasdaq 100 remained flat.

title: Apple Earnings Preview: Can It Keep Winning? Cook’s Final Quarter Steals Focus
summary: Apple reports Q2 2026 earnings on April 30, with Wall Street expecting $109.46B in revenue and $1.95 EPS. Key focus is on whether Apple Intelligence can drive sustained iPhone upgrade cycles and the impact of CEO succession as John Ternus takes over from Tim Cook in September. Services segment growth and iPhone 17 demand, particularly in China, will be closely watched.

title: Microsoft's Cloud Beat Lands, But AI Stock Laggard Still Has Something To Prove
summary: Microsoft delivered better-than-expected Q3 earnings with Azure revenue growing 40% and improved operating margins, but the stock fell 5.95% as investors remain skeptical. Despite strong cloud and AI infrastructure demand, experts note Microsoft has underperformed expectations as an AI winner, with concerns about hardware capacity constraints and lack of meaningful surprises to drive sentiment change.

title: S&P 500 Edges Higher Amid Mixed Mega-Cap Earnings; Dow Leads Market Indexes Overall
summary: U.S. stock indexes rose on April 30, 2026, with the Dow leading gains driven by Caterpillar's 10% surge on strong earnings. Mega-cap tech earnings were mixed: Alphabet soared 9.6% on robust Google Cloud revenue growth, while Meta and Microsoft fell on concerns about massive AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia declined 4.3% amid competition concerns. The market showed investors are now scrutinizing which companies convert AI hype into actual revenue.

title: 3 Stocks I'd Rather Own Than Apple With a CEO Shakeup
summary: With Tim Cook stepping down as Apple CEO in September 2026 and John Ternus taking over, the article argues that leadership transitions create uncertainty. Apple trades at a premium valuation (34x earnings) without strong growth prospects and lacks a clear AI strategy. The author recommends Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet as better investment alternatives due to their strong AI exposure, cloud computing growth, and more attractive valuations.

title: Amazon’s Earnings Just Sent the Stock to New Highs—What’s Next?
summary: Amazon's stock hit all-time highs following strong earnings that beat expectations on revenue and earnings. AWS growth accelerated to 28% year-over-year, driven by AI and cloud infrastructure demand. The company demonstrated that AI investments are translating into meaningful returns. However, with a 35% rally in over a month and high analyst price targets, the stock now faces a higher bar for continued growth, requiring sustained momentum to justify current valuations.

title: Prediction: These Will Be the Next $5 Trillion Companies
summary: The article predicts that Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon will become $5 trillion companies, following Nvidia's achievement. Their cloud computing businesses, powered by AI demand, are positioned to drive massive growth. Alphabet needs less than 20% growth to reach the target, while Microsoft could benefit from valuation expansion, and Amazon's highly profitable AWS segment generates most operating income.

title: MongoDB Could Be Setting Up for a Sharp Earnings Rebound
summary: MongoDB's stock has been oversold due to market overreaction to AI disruption fears and cautious Q1 2026 guidance, despite strong Q4 2025 results and robust full-year outlook. With analysts setting a low bar and institutional support, the upcoming late May earnings release could trigger significant upside, potentially exceeding 100% as the market recognizes MongoDB's competitive advantages in AI applications through its Atlas platform.

title: Alphabet Earnings Didn’t Just Beat—They Changed the Story
summary: Alphabet delivered exceptional Q1 2026 results with 22% revenue growth to $109.9B, beating estimates across all major metrics. Google Cloud was the standout performer with 63% YoY growth and $20.03B in revenue, while Search queries hit all-time highs. The company raised CapEx guidance to $180-190B, signaling continued aggressive AI investment. With a $460B cloud backlog and 350M paid subscriptions, analysts expect price target revisions.

title: Stock Market Today, April 30: U.S. Markets Surge Higher Despite a Mixed Bag of Earnings From Big Tech
summary: U.S. markets rose on April 30, 2026, with the S&P 500 gaining 1.02%, Nasdaq up 0.89%, and Dow jumping 1.62%. Alphabet surged 10% on strong earnings and AI commentary, while Microsoft and Meta declined 4% and 9% respectively due to concerns over massive AI capital expenditure. Caterpillar also rallied 10% on robust results, helping fuel the Dow's gains.

title: Stock Market Today, April 30: Meta Falls as Higher AI Capex Outlook Overshadows Strong Q1 Results
summary: Meta's stock fell 8.6% despite beating Q1 earnings expectations, as investors reacted negatively to the company's sharply increased AI and data center capital expenditure guidance, potentially reaching $145 billion in 2026. The market is concerned whether Meta's ad pricing, engagement, and Reels monetization improvements can offset the rising infrastructure costs and protect margins.

title: Here's Why This Remains My Least Favorite "Magnificent Seven" Stock -- Even After a Strong Earnings Report
summary: Despite Microsoft's strong Q3 2026 earnings with 18% revenue growth and a $37 billion AI business run rate, analyst Daniel Sparks remains bearish on the stock. Azure's growth of 39% shows minimal acceleration compared to competitors, while AWS and Google Cloud are reaccelerating sharply. Additionally, AI threatens to disrupt Microsoft's profitable per-seat Office licensing model, and the company's revised OpenAI exclusivity deal weakens a key AI advantage.

title: While "Magnificent Seven" Companies Pour Hundreds of Billions into AI Infrastructure, Apple Continues to Execute the Classic Shareholder-Friendly Playbook
summary: Apple reported Q2 2026 earnings that beat estimates, raising its quarterly dividend by 4% to $0.27 per share and authorizing a $100 billion share repurchase program. While other 'Magnificent Seven' companies like Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta are investing heavily in AI infrastructure with capex exceeding $100 billion annually, Apple continues its traditional shareholder-friendly approach, having repurchased $37 billion in stock and distributed $7.7 billion in dividends in the first half of fiscal 2026.
